These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

Institutions described by the Nation

The Nation identifies executive, legislative, judicial and general council branches, referring to its 1963 and 1994 constitutions. It also distinguishes a traditional chief-and-clan system. These institutional descriptions introduce a named government within wider Ho-Chunk history. They are not a substitute for reading current governing texts, and they do not identify the Wisconsin Nation with every other Ho-Chunk government.

Read the sources [1] Ho-Chunk Nation

02

Preservation and language as public responsibilities

Heritage Preservation describes research, archives, conservation and education as responsibilities carried through the Nation’s own institutions. Its Language Division emphasizes continuity across generations. Together these statements show stewardship as ongoing community work. They describe purposes and responsibilities; they do not measure language fluency, establish the accessibility of every collection or make protected knowledge public.

Read the sources [2] Ho-Chunk Nation
